title: How planes fly
examples: Teacher, what is the difference between lift and weight?
Can you explain how the shape of the wing helps the plane?
What does the angle of attack really change?

explain.say: Today we are learning how airplanes stay up in the sky.
The first force is lift, which pushes the plane up into the air.
Weight is the force pulling the plane straight down towards the ground.
Thrust is the force generated by the engines pushing the plane forward.
Drag is the force that resists the plane's movement through the air.
The curved shape of the wing, called an airfoil, is very important.

faq.q: Does lift only come from the curved top of the wing?
faq.a: No, lift is created by the air moving over and under the wing. The shape helps manage this airflow.
asks: Where does the lift actually come from?
Is the curve the only thing that makes lift?

faq.q: If I increase the angle of attack, what happens to the lift?
faq.a: Increasing the angle of attack generally increases the lift until a certain point is reached. Too much can cause a stall.
asks: What is the best angle for lift?
Does the angle affect the lift amount?

faq.q: Are thrust and drag always opposite forces?
faq.a: Yes, thrust pushes the plane forward, and drag pushes backward, so they are always opposing each other.
asks: How do thrust and drag relate?
Do they always work against each other?

faq.q: What is the angle of attack in simple terms?
faq.a: It is the angle between the wing and the oncoming air flow. It is measured in degrees.
asks: How do I measure the angle of attack?
What is the angle between the wing and air?

faq.q: Do planes need to balance lift and weight to fly?
faq.a: Yes, for steady flight, the lift generated must balance the weight of the plane. This keeps the plane level.
asks: What must lift equal for level flight?
How do I keep the plane from falling?

facts: Lift is created by differences in air pressure over the wing.
Thrust is the forward force provided by the engines.
Drag is the force that slows the plane down.
The angle of attack is the angle between the wing and the relative wind.

quiz.say: If a plane is flying straight and level, which forces must balance?
quiz.why: When flying level, the upward lift must perfectly balance the downward weight.

wrong.1: While this is true for level flight, the question asks about the vertical balance.
wrong.2: Lift is vertical, and thrust is horizontal, so they do not directly balance each other.
wrong.3: Weight is vertical, and drag is horizontal, so they do not balance each other.

quiz.say: What force pushes the plane forward through the air?
quiz.why: The engines create a powerful forward push called thrust.

wrong.0: Drag is the force that tries to slow the plane down.
wrong.2: Lift is the upward force that keeps the plane airborne.
wrong.3: Weight is the force pulling the plane down towards Earth.

quiz.say: If a plane increases its angle of attack, what is the most likely immediate effect on lift?

options.show: Lift will immediately drop to zero
options.say: Lift will immediately drop to zero

options.show: Lift will decrease because of drag
options.say: Lift will decrease because of drag

quiz.why: Increasing the angle of attack increases the pressure difference, thus increasing lift.

wrong.0: This only happens at a stall, not immediately upon increasing the angle.
wrong.1: While drag increases, the primary effect of a small increase in angle is more lift.
wrong.2: Aerodynamics follows predictable principles based on the angle used.
